value.text: At source level, start subscribes to weather.place-requested and weather.forecast-updated from the beginning and runs consumeMessage with autoCommit false; this does not prove runtime activation or delivery. The saved mapping of weather.place-requested to consumeMessage is agent-proposed. For this topic, validateEvent requires a string event id, version 1, an allowed place id, string name, finite coordinates, type place.requested, and no forecast. The known forecast-updated topic has its own validator branch; only an unrecognized topic name throws UNKNOWN_TOPIC, and consumeMessage catches that too as INVALID_EVENT. On parse or validation failure it writes a rejected_messages row and commits offset plus one; a write or commit failure propagates. On valid input it inserts the event id into inbox within a transaction; an existing id commits and returns DUPLICATE without changing the card, while a new place event upserts name and coordinates without replacing forecast data. If the DB transaction commits but offset commit then fails, a replay can occur; inbox suppresses duplicate application, not delivery, so this is not exactly-once processing. If pool.connect succeeds, errors inside applyEvent’s try attempt rollback, rethrow, and release in finally. A connection failure occurs before the try, so no transaction rollback or client release runs; either failure prevents offset commit. Runtime behavior remains unverified.
